title: लुम्बिनी विकास कोषमा आवेदन नै नदिएका व्यक्ति पदाधिकारी नियुक्त
content:
No ads found for this position रुपन्देही । सरकारले लुम्बिनी विकास कोषको पदाधिकारीमा आवेदन नै नदिएका व्यक्तिलाई कार्यकारी पद सुम्पेको छ । यसअघि इच्छुक र विज्ञहरुलाई सम्बन्धित पदमा आवेदन मागेर सरकारले खुला प्रतिस्पर्धाबाट सार्वजनिक पदमा जिम्मेवारी दिन खोजेको भन्दै प्रशंसा भएको थियो तर नियुक्त दिने समयमा भने त्यसलाई बेवास्ता गर्दै आन्तरिक रुपमै निकटस्थहरुलाई जिम्मेवारी दिइएको हो । मंगलबार मात्रै आवेदन नै नदिएका भौतिक पूर्वाधार मन्त्री सुनिल लम्सालका प्रमुख सल्लाहकार सन्तोष पाण्डेय लुम्बिनी विकास कोषको सदस्यसचिव नियुक्त भएका हुन् । सामाजिक सन्जालमा सरकारले बाहिर प्रचारमा एउटा कुरा गर्ने र भित्र अर्कै ढंगले काम गर्ने भन्दै आलोचना सुरु भएको छ । सरकारले पुनः पहुँचका आधारमा नेतृत्व नियुक्त गरेको भन्द्रै सुशासनका विषयमा सार्वजनिक अभिव्यक्ति आइरहेका छन् । खुला प्रतिस्पर्धाबाट पदाधिकारी छनोट गर्ने प्रक्रिया अघि बढाए पनि सरकारले प्रतिस्पर्धामा सहभागी नै नभएका पूर्वाधार विकासमन्त्री सुनील लम्सालका प्रमुख सल्लाहकार सन्तोष पाण्डेलाई सदस्यसचिव नियुक्त गरेको हो। कोषका सदस्यसचिवसहित विभिन्न ६ पदका लागि ७ सय २७ जनाले आवेदन दिएका थिए। उपलब्ध आधिकारिक रोस्टर सूचीअनुसार सदस्यसचिव पदका लागि २ सय ९६, सदस्य पदका लागि २ सय २३, योजना प्रमुखका लागि १ सय १०, उपाध्यक्षका लागि १ सय २ र कोषाध्यक्षका लागि ७१ जनाले आवेदन दिएका थिए। तर, मन्त्रिपरिषद्ले आवेदकलाई प्रतिस्पर्धामा सहभागी नगराउनुकै सट्टा रोस्टरमा नामसमेत नभएका पाण्डेलाई सदस्यसचिव नियुक्त गरेपछि सरकारको निर्णयको आलोचना भएको छ। मंगलबार बसेको मन्त्रिपरिषद् बैठकले पाण्डेलाई सदस्यसचिव नियुक्त गर्नुका साथै अन्य ४ जनालाई परिषद् सदस्यमा मनोनयन गरेको छ। नियुक्त हुने परिषद् सदस्यमा डा. अमित केसी, अर्जुन कुमी, उपेक्षा गुरुङ र दीपक कौशल छन्। नवनियुक्त सदस्य अर्जुन कुमीले आफूहरूले नियुक्तिपत्रसमेत बुझिसकेको जानकारी दिए। ५ पदाधिकारीमध्ये रोस्टर सूचीबाट खुला प्रतिस्पर्धामा सहभागी भएका अर्जुन कुमी (क्रमसंख्या ५५०) र भिक्षुणी उपेक्षा गुरुङ (क्रमसंख्या ५४२) मात्रै छनोट भएका छन्। सदस्यसचिव पाण्डे, डा. अमित केसी र दीपक कौशलको नाम भने मन्त्रालयले सार्वजनिक गरेको आधिकारिक रोस्टरमा छैन। उनीहरूले खुला प्रतिस्पर्धाका लागि आवेदन दिएको थिएनन्। यसअघि असोज ३० गतेको मन्त्रिपरिषद् बैठकले उपाध्यक्षमा गायिका आनी छोइड डोल्मालाई नियुक्त गर्दा पनि प्रक्रिया र मापदण्ड मिचिएको भन्दै विरोध भएको थियो। उपाध्यक्ष पदका लागि रोष्टरमा १ सय ३ जना भए पनि प्रतिस्पर्धामा सहभागी नभएकी डोल्मालाई नियुक्त गरिएको भन्दै आलोचना भएको थियो। लुम्बिनी बचाउ महाअभियानका सल्लाहकार दिनेश त्रिपाठीले नियुक्ति प्रक्रियाप्रति विरोध जनाएका छन्। अभियानका सहसंयोजक रामविकास चौधरीले लुम्बिनीको गरिमा अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय स्तरमा उकास्न, पुरातात्त्विक सम्पदा जोगाउन र अलपत्र गुरुयोजनाको काम सम्पन्न गर्न सक्षम तथा निष्पक्ष विज्ञ आवश्यक रहेको बताए। उनले खुला प्रतिस्पर्धाबाट आएका सबै उम्मेदवारलाई पन्छाएर रोस्टरबाहिरका व्यक्तिलाई नियुक्त गर्नुले लुम्बिनी विकास कोषलाई राजनीतिक स्वार्थ समूहको अड्डा बनाउने नियत देखिएको आरोप लगाए। सत्तारुढ राष्ट्रिय स्वतन्त्र पार्टी (रास्वपा)का निकटस्थहरुले भने लुम्बिनी विकास कोषमा विज्ञ आवश्य भएको र आवेदनमा परेकाहरु भन्दा बाहिरबाट नियुक्त भएको दावी गरेका छन् । Rupandehi. The government has given the executive position of the Lumbini Development Fund to a person who did not even apply. Earlier, the government was praised for seeking applications from interested and experts for relevant positions and for trying to assign responsibilities in public positions through open competition, but at the time of making appointments, this was ignored and responsibilities were given internally to those close to them. Santosh Pandey, chief advisor to Physical Infrastructure Minister Sunil Lamsal, who did not even apply on Tuesday, has been appointed as member secretary of the Lumbini Development Fund. Criticism has begun on social media that the government is doing one thing in public relations and doing something else internally. The government has again been making public statements about good governance, as it has appointed leaders based on access. Although the process of selecting office bearers through open competition has been initiated, the government has appointed Santosh Pandey, the chief advisor to Infrastructure Development Minister Sunil Lamsal, who did not participate in the competition, as member secretary. A total of 727 people had applied for six different positions, including the member secretary of the fund. According to the available official roster list, 296 people had applied for the member secretary position, 223 for the member position, 110 for the project head, 102 for the vice-chairman, and 71 for the treasurer. However, the government's decision has been criticized after the cabinet appointed Pandey, whose name was not even on the roster, as the member secretary instead of excluding the applicant from the competition. The cabinet meeting held on Tuesday appointed Pandey as member secretary and nominated four others as council members. The council members to be appointed are Dr. Amit KC, Arjun Kumi, Upeksha Gurung and Deepak Kaushal. Newly appointed member Arjun Kumi informed that they have also received the appointment letter. Of the 5 office bearers, only Arjun Kumi (serial number 550) and Bhikshuni Upeksha Gurung (serial number 542) who participated in the open competition have been selected from the roster list. The names of Member Secretary Pandey, Dr. Amit KC and Deepak Kaushal are not on the official roster made public by the ministry. They had not applied for the open competition. Earlier, there was protest against the appointment of singer Ani Choid Dolma as Vice President at the Cabinet meeting on October 10, saying that the process and criteria were violated. There was criticism that Dolma, who did not participate in the competition, was appointed even though there were 103 people on the roster for the position of Vice President. Lumbini Save Campaign advisor Dinesh Tripathi has expressed his opposition to the appointment process. Campaign co-coordinator Ram Bikas Chaudhary said that competent and impartial experts are needed to elevate Lumbini's prestige at the international level, protect its archaeological heritage, and complete the pending master plan. He alleged that appointing someone outside the roster, bypassing all candidates who came through open competition, shows an intention to make the Lumbini Development Fund a base for political interest groups. Those close to the ruling National Independent Party (NISP), however, have claimed that experts were needed in the Lumbini Development Fund and that they were appointed from outside the applicants.

The government has given the executive position of the Lumbini Development Fund to a person who did not even apply. Earlier, the government was praised for seeking applications from interested and experts for relevant positions and for trying to assign responsibilities in public positions through open competition, but at the time of making appointments, this was ignored and responsibilities were given internally to those close to them. Santosh Pandey, chief advisor to Physical Infrastructure Minister Sunil Lamsal, who did not even apply on Tuesday, has been appointed as member secretary of the Lumbini Development Fund. Criticism has begun on social media that the government is doing one thing in public relations and doing something else internally. The government has again been making public statements about good governance, as it has appointed leaders based on access. Although the process of selecting office bearers through open competition has been initiated, the government has appointed Santosh Pandey, the chief advisor to Infrastructure Development Minister Sunil Lamsal, who did not participate in the competition, as member secretary. A total of 727 people had applied for six different positions, including the member secretary of the fund. According to the available official roster list, 296 people had applied for the member secretary position, 223 for the member position, 110 for the project head, 102 for the vice-chairman, and 71 for the treasurer. However, the government's decision has been criticized after the cabinet appointed Pandey, whose name was not even on the roster, as the member secretary instead of excluding the applicant from the competition. The cabinet meeting held on Tuesday appointed Pandey as member secretary and nominated four others as council members. The council members to be appointed are Dr. Amit KC, Arjun Kumi, Upeksha Gurung and Deepak Kaushal. Newly appointed member Arjun Kumi informed that they have also received the appointment letter. Of the 5 office bearers, only Arjun Kumi (serial number 550) and Bhikshuni Upeksha Gurung (serial number 542) who participated in the open competition have been selected from the roster list. The names of Member Secretary Pandey, Dr. Amit KC and Deepak Kaushal are not on the official roster made public by the ministry. They had not applied for the open competition. Earlier, there was protest against the appointment of singer Ani Choid Dolma as Vice President at the Cabinet meeting on October 10, saying that the process and criteria were violated. There was criticism that Dolma, who did not participate in the competition, was appointed even though there were 103 people on the roster for the position of Vice President. Lumbini Save Campaign advisor Dinesh Tripathi has expressed his opposition to the appointment process. Campaign co-coordinator Ram Bikas Chaudhary said that competent and impartial experts are needed to elevate Lumbini's prestige at the international level, protect its archaeological heritage, and complete the pending master plan. He alleged that appointing someone outside the roster, bypassing all candidates who came through open competition, shows an intention to make the Lumbini Development Fund a base for political interest groups. Those close to the ruling National Independent Party (NISP), however, have claimed that experts were needed in the Lumbini Development Fund and that they were appointed from outside the applicants.

The government has given the executive position of the Lumbini Development Fund to a person who did not even apply. Santosh Pandey, chief advisor to Physical Infrastructure Minister Sunil Lamsal, who did not even apply on Tuesday, has been appointed as member secretary of the Lumbini Development Fund. Criticism has begun on social media that the government is doing one thing in public relations and doing something else internally. The government has again been making public statements about good governance, as it has appointed leaders based on access. Although the process of selecting office bearers through open competition has been initiated, the government has appointed Santosh Pandey, the chief advisor to Infrastructure Development Minister Sunil Lamsal, who did not participate in the competition, as member secretary. A total of 727 people had applied for six different positions, including the member secretary of the fund. According to the available official roster list, 296 people had applied for the member secretary position, 223 for the member position, 110 for the project head, 102 for the vice-chairman, and 71 for the treasurer. The cabinet meeting held on Tuesday appointed Pandey as member secretary and nominated four others as council members. Earlier, there was protest against the appointment of singer Ani Choid Dolma as Vice President at the Cabinet meeting on October 10, saying that the process and criteria were violated. There was criticism that Dolma, who did not participate in the competition, was appointed even though there were 103 people on the roster for the position of Vice President. Lumbini Save Campaign advisor Dinesh Tripathi has expressed his opposition to the appointment process. Campaign co-coordinator Ram Bikas Chaudhary said that competent and impartial experts are needed to elevate Lumbini's prestige at the international level, protect its archaeological heritage, and complete the pending master plan. He alleged that appointing someone outside the roster, bypassing all candidates who came through open competition, shows an intention to make the Lumbini Development Fund a base for political interest groups. Those close to the ruling National Independent Party (NISP), however, have claimed that experts were needed in the Lumbini Development Fund and that they were appointed from outside the applicants.

मंगलबार बसेको मन्त्रिपरिषद् बैठकले पाण्डेलाई सदस्यसचिव नियुक्त गर्नुका साथै अन्य ४ जनालाई परिषद् सदस्यमा मनोनयन गरेको छ। नियुक्त हुने परिषद् सदस्यमा डा. अमित केसी, अर्जुन कुमी, उपेक्षा गुरुङ र दीपक कौशल छन्। नवनियुक्त सदस्य अर्जुन कुमीले आफूहरूले नियुक्तिपत्रसमेत बुझिसकेको जानकारी दिए।

५ पदाधिकारीमध्ये रोस्टर सूचीबाट खुला प्रतिस्पर्धामा सहभागी भएका अर्जुन कुमी (क्रमसंख्या ५५०) र भिक्षुणी उपेक्षा गुरुङ (क्रमसंख्या ५४२) मात्रै छनोट भएका छन्। सदस्यसचिव पाण्डे, डा. अमित केसी र दीपक कौशलको नाम भने मन्त्रालयले सार्वजनिक गरेको आधिकारिक रोस्टरमा छैन। उनीहरूले खुला प्रतिस्पर्धाका लागि आवेदन दिएको थिएनन्।

यसअघि असोज ३० गतेको मन्त्रिपरिषद् बैठकले उपाध्यक्षमा गायिका आनी छोइड डोल्मालाई नियुक्त गर्दा पनि प्रक्रिया र मापदण्ड मिचिएको भन्दै विरोध भएको थियो। उपाध्यक्ष पदका लागि रोष्टरमा १ सय ३ जना भए पनि प्रतिस्पर्धामा सहभागी नभएकी डोल्मालाई नियुक्त गरिएको भन्दै आलोचना भएको थियो।

लुम्बिनी बचाउ महाअभियानका सल्लाहकार दिनेश त्रिपाठीले नियुक्ति प्रक्रियाप्रति विरोध जनाएका छन्। अभियानका सहसंयोजक रामविकास चौधरीले लुम्बिनीको गरिमा अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय स्तरमा उकास्न, पुरातात्त्विक सम्पदा जोगाउन र अलपत्र गुरुयोजनाको काम सम्पन्न गर्न सक्षम तथा निष्पक्ष विज्ञ आवश्यक रहेको बताए।

उनले खुला प्रतिस्पर्धाबाट आएका सबै उम्मेदवारलाई पन्छाएर रोस्टरबाहिरका व्यक्तिलाई नियुक्त गर्नुले लुम्बिनी विकास कोषलाई राजनीतिक स्वार्थ समूहको अड्डा बनाउने नियत देखिएको आरोप लगाए।

सत्तारुढ राष्ट्रिय स्वतन्त्र पार्टी (रास्वपा)का निकटस्थहरुले भने लुम्बिनी विकास कोषमा विज्ञ आवश्य भएको र आवेदनमा परेकाहरु भन्दा बाहिरबाट नियुक्त भएको दावी गरेका छन् ।

Santosh Pandey, chief advisor to Physical Infrastructure Minister Sunil Lamsal, who did not even apply on Tuesday, has been appointed as member secretary of the Lumbini Development Fund. According to the available official roster list, 296 people had applied for the member secretary position, 223 for the member position, 110 for the project head, 102 for the vice-chairman, and 71 for the treasurer. However, the government's decision has been criticized after the cabinet appointed Pandey, whose name was not even on the roster, as the member secretary instead of excluding the applicant from the competition. The cabinet meeting held on Tuesday appointed Pandey as member secretary and nominated four others as council members. Of the 5 office bearers, only Arjun Kumi (serial number 550) and Bhikshuni Upeksha Gurung (serial number 542) who participated in the open competition have been selected from the roster list. The names of Member Secretary Pandey, Dr. Amit KC and Deepak Kaushal are not on the official roster made public by the ministry. They had not applied for the open competition. Earlier, there was protest against the appointment of singer Ani Choid Dolma as Vice President at the Cabinet meeting on October 10, saying that the process and criteria were violated. There was criticism that Dolma, who did not participate in the competition, was appointed even though there were 103 people on the roster for the position of Vice President. Lumbini Save Campaign advisor Dinesh Tripathi has expressed his opposition to the appointment process. Campaign co-coordinator Ram Bikas Chaudhary said that competent and impartial experts are needed to elevate Lumbini's prestige at the international level, protect its archaeological heritage, and complete the pending master plan. He alleged that appointing someone outside the roster, bypassing all candidates who came through open competition, shows an intention to make the Lumbini Development Fund a base for political interest groups. Those close to the ruling National Independent Party (NISP), however, have claimed that experts were needed in the Lumbini Development Fund and that they were appointed from outside the applicants.
